reading.body:
This King of Prussia facility is a 22,000 square-foot site with 4 MW of published power capacity. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a standard AI training density, 4 MW of IT load translates to roughly 100 racks. The site is modest in absolute terms and ranks fourth among the four Pennsylvania facilities that publish power figures, accounting for 18 percent of the state's 22.2 MW of disclosed data center capacity.

No certifications qualify this site for specific workload classes. The operator publishes only floor space and power, not tenant names, cooling architecture, network connectivity, or grid interconnection details that would clarify whether this capacity serves AI training, inference, or other uses.

Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data center facilities of which only four disclose megawatt figures, making this campus one of very few in the state with public technical specifications. Whether the state's unmapped or non-publishing sites hold larger capacity remains unknown from published sources.
